transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Samir Patel (Redwood); Karen Lewis, Devon Price, Ravi Menon, Aisha Rahman (Synergy Care)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Luis our CSM and Samir our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Karen: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get started.
[00:12] Devon: Yeah, appreciate you all. We're looking to get Redwood into a pilot by end of month if possible.
[00:18] Maya: Great, that's what today's for — align on timeline, who's doing what, and the security checks so we can unblock a pilot. I'll hand to Luis for a quick run of the onboarding steps, then Samir will go into integration options.
[00:29] Luis: Thanks. High-level we usually run a 3-week pilot: week 1 is infra and access, week 2 is integration and smoke tests, week 3 is load/quality checks and evaluation. Typical items we need from you: network access (VPC peering or private link), service account for API keys or SSO, and a few representative prompts/workloads.
[00:44] Ravi: For us security is primary. We need to understand data residency, encryption at rest and in transit, and how KMS works for private deployments. Also audit logging and retention.
[00:55] Aisha: Yes we need SOC 2 type II evidence and any certifications plus how you handle tenant isolation if we're on dedicated capacity or private.
[01:05] Samir: Absolutely — we support hosted API for quicker onboarding, dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for stricter controls. For the pilot we usually recommend hosted first unless you require VPC straight away. Hosted can be set up with private logging and KMS integration depending on your compliance posture.
[01:22] Devon: Hmm, we prefer to keep PHI inside our environment. We might need private or at least VPC peering. Is that available for pilots?
[01:30] Samir: Yes, we can do VPC peering for pilot accounts. There's some networking prep — route tables, subnets, security groups — but it's usually straightforward. For strictly on-prem air-gapped we have a different process but that's more involved.
[01:45] Karen: Also want visibility into cost and latency — our product team cares about p95 latency under 300ms for small prompts, and cost per 1k tokens needs to be estimated.
[01:55] Maya: We'll share our cost model and latency benchmarks. Samir, can you speak to batching/kv cache and how that impacts latency vs cost?
[02:03] Samir: Sure — Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and prefix/KV caching; that improves throughput and lowers per-token cost but can add a small tail latency if you wait for batch windows. We tune batch size and max latency to match SLOs. For low-latency interactive workloads we configure small batch windows and higher priority routing. For bulk inference we use larger batches.
[02:20] Karen: Ok, so for our chat assistant product low tail latency is more important during conversation flows, but for nightly summarization batch cost matters. We need both.
[02:30] Luis: That's common. For the pilot we can instrument two routes: one tuned for chat (low latency) and one for bulk processing (cost optimized). We'll show you dashboarding in the console for token-level cost and per-route SLOs.
[02:42] Devon: On the network side, Ravi will handle provisioning. Ravi, do you have a timeline for network infra?
[02:48] Ravi: I can have a test VPC and role created by Monday 12/20, need exact subnet ranges and a short list of IPs. Also need a runbook for the peering steps.
[02:56] Samir: We'll send a sample infra diagram and the peering instructions. We'll need a security contact to validate firewall rules.
[03:04] Aisha: I'll be that contact. I want the list of logs and retention periods up front.
[03:09] Maya: Great — action item for us to send the onboarding runbook, security docs, and the SSO/SAML guide.
[03:15] Karen: One more question: we have an internal model evaluation suite. Can you support a rollback/ A/B traffic split if quality regressions occur?
[03:23] Samir: Yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallbacks to model variants, and evaluation hooks. We can integrate your eval harness to trigger alerts on regression. We also provide quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[03:36] Devon: For the pilot success criteria, we want p95 latency < 300ms on chat route, throughput to handle 50 rps during peak tests, and no PII leakage in the outputs. Also we need logs and audit trails for any access.
[03:50] Luis: I'll capture those as the pilot success criteria and share a doc.
[03:54] Maya: Awesome. On pricing, we'll share a pilot pricing note — typical pilot credits and how usage maps to the hosted/ dedicated model.
[04:02] Karen: Competitors we evaluated included Anthropic and an in-house inference stack but Redwood's routing and observability are compelling.
[04:10] Maya: Thank you. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[04:14] Luis: Next steps: Maya sends runbook and security docs by 12/17; Ravi configures test VPC and shares details by 12/20; Luis and Devon schedule pilot window by 12/22 and Luis will circulate pilot success criteria.
[04:28] Karen: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[04:31] Ravi: None on our side once I get the peering instructions.
[04:34] Aisha: I'll review the SOC2 artifacts when you send them.
[04:36] Maya: Perfect. We'll set up a follow-up check-in for the week of 12/27 to review results from the pilot run. Thanks everyone.
[04:44] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker overlaps and a few misrecognized acronyms (KMS sometimes transcribed as "K M S"). References to product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console. Shared artifacts: onboarding_runbook.pdf (link sent after meeting), pilot_pricing_notes.xlsx (to follow), infra_peering_template.txt.
